text.text_excerpt: I love this place! I was so excited to find another French bakery! The decor is so pretty. It's a cute little place for afternoon tea or coffee date :) My favorite so far are the Mille Feuilles, cream puff, the quiches, and croissant sandwich. The chocolate eclair was good, but a little too rich for me. I might try the regular cream filling next time. The strawberry tart was good, but a little too sweet for my taste. This was actually my second visit this week because I wanted to try everything. You can definitely taste all the love in their pastries. This has been one of my favorite places outside of Europe for French Pastries so far.

What a great place! I purchased a mocha and a piece of galette de rois (the French version of king cake). The mocha was not my taste (the coffee was bitter and I like my drink sweeter). However, the pastry was delicious! The decor included original NOLA art and beautiful flowers all over the walls. There are many pastry, dessert, sandwich, breakfast/lunch, and drink choices. Inside and outside seating available. Both street and lot parking available. And incredibly, a handicap accessible ramp into the building! I will definitely be back, the staff was friendly and helpful. Everyone was wearing masks and following covid protocols.

What a charming, chic little neighborhood French Bakery. They're located on Robert E. Lee, and there's a parking lot behind the building. The case is filled with rich looking, gorgeous pastries and there are several varieties of breads behind the counter. There are a few tables inside so that you can sit and relax while you enjoy your treats. On this visit I picked up a few things to go - a baguette, a chocolate croissant, and a cup of hot cocoa. The pastries were every bit as good as any pastries I've had in Paris. The cocoa was very tasty, but not as thick as a French hot chocolate. I'm looking forward to making my way through the entire pastry case in time.
